title: regime_overhaul: /frameworksInScope
description: rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 is still in frameworksInScope, but for NBFCs RBI repealed it on 28 Nov 2025. It was replaced by the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/363). Chapter IV and the IT-specific provisions of Chapter II apply to NBFCs in the Middle Layer and above, and this entity's RBI registration N-13.09999 is nbfc-middle-layer. The successor has no vocab id and no instruments.json entry lists rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 in supersedes[], so instrument_superseded cannot be expressed. The profile is left unchanged and the regime change is flagged for re-review. Timing caveat: the repeal predates the catalog retrievedAt (2026-09-14), and the catalog version string already records it. It is reported because the profile was never refreshed and the repeal falls inside the 24-month window. Third-party IT and cyber arrangements outside the outsourcing directions fall under rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026 paras 126-135, which is already in scope. From: rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 (in scope as a binding instrument). To: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025, RBI/DOR/2025-26/363 (no vocab id). Effective date: 2025-11-28.

description: src/tools/args.ts's zEJSON() (lines 78-90, used for find/export filters and every non-vector-search aggregation stage) is `z.object({}).loose()` with no maxItems on the enclosing pipeline array and no maxLength/pattern on keys or values; DBOperationArgs.database and CollOperationArgs.collection (mongodbTool.ts:11-17) are plain z.string() with no length cap or character allow-list, unlike CommonArgs.string()'s NO_UNICODE_REGEX in the same repo (args.ts:22-23). This is an input-validation gap on the tool-call surface, not a rate-limiting mechanism, which this codebase does not implement at all for MCP tool calls.

title: MongoDB MCP tool schemas carry no personal-data classification markers
description: src/tools/mongodb/mongodbSchemas.ts:1-107 (and, by extension, every mongodb/* tool argsShape it feeds) defines filter, projection, document and pipeline fields as opaque EJSON or `.passthrough()` records with only a `.describe()` prose hint (e.g. `zAutoEmbedVectorSearchStageParams`, `VectorSearchStage`). No field, in this file or anywhere under src/tools/mongodb, carries a data-classification annotation (x-data-classification, x-dpdp-category, @pii or equivalent), although applications/mcp-gateway/README.md and applications/mcp-gateway/env/{qa,prod}.json declare the connected client-data and order stores pii + financial. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0. zEJSON is defined as z.object({}).loose() in src/tools/args.ts:88-90; .passthrough() appears only in find.ts:22 and create/createIndex.ts:164, not in mongodbSchemas.ts itself.

title: find tool returns full unmasked documents from pii/financial collections
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/find.ts:108-118: FindTool.execute EJSON-serialises the entire cursor result set (`EJSON.stringify(cursorResults.documents)`) and returns it verbatim to the MCP client; the only applied limits are `config.maxBytesPerQuery` and `config.maxDocumentsPerQuery`, neither of which masks or filters fields. env/qa.json and env/prod.json both declare dataClassification [pii, financial] for this app. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: aggregate tool returns full unmasked pipeline results
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/aggregate.ts:187-192: AggregateTool.execute EJSON-serialises and returns the entire aggregation result set for an arbitrary user-supplied pipeline; pipelines containing `$out`/`$merge` (lines 134-141) write to a collection and send back no documents, so they are not an additional data-return path, but the read branch's result set still carries no masking or classification filter before being returned to the client. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: export tool writes full unmasked documents to an unencrypted local file
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/export.ts:68-98: ExportTool.execute streams the full find/aggregate cursor to a local JSON file via ExportsManager.createJSONExport with no field mask and no encryption-at-rest on the export file; the file is exposed to the caller via a resource URI and, on stdio transport (isServerRunningLocally(), lines 131-133), its plain filesystem path. Cleanup relies on ExportsManager.close() deleting the session export directory and a best-effort TTL sweep (config.exportTimeoutMs, default 300000ms), not immediate purge. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: CreateDBUserTool returns a newly generated password in plain text
description: src/tools/atlas/create/createDBUser.ts:84-96: when the tool auto-generates a password, the success content text is `User "${username}" created successfully with password: \`${password}\`.`, sent as the raw JSON-RPC tool result. `this.session.keychain.register(password, "password")` runs immediately before, but keychain-based redaction (loggerBase.ts) only scrubs subsequent logger output, not the direct tool-result payload that reaches the MCP client transcript. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: MCP HTTP transport has no default authentication requirement
description: src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:306-319: setupMiddlewares() is the only request gate on the HTTP transport; it loops over `Object.entries(this.userConfig.httpHeaders)` and rejects a request only if a configured header value mismatches. `httpHeaders` defaults to `{}` (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:136-143), so with no operator configuration the loop performs zero comparisons and `next()` is always called: every JSON-RPC tool call is reachable unauthenticated over HTTP once the transport binds beyond loopback (httpHost defaults to 127.0.0.1; the repo's AWS Dockerfile sets host 0.0.0.0 and the Azure bicep binds to '::'). Consistent with this, deploy/azure/bicep/params_template.json ships `authMode: NOAUTH` by default; a proper Azure-AD OIDC auth config exists only as an opt-in second template. env/prod.json lists this app's prod environment as exposure: partner with dataClassification [pii, financial]. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: Core MongoDB tool arguments accept unbounded, unvalidated input that reaches the driver
description: src/tools/args.ts:78-90: `zEJSON()` (`z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON)`) accepts any key/value pair with no maxItems on enclosing arrays (AggregateArgs.pipeline, defined at src/tools/mongodb/read/aggregate.ts:47-49) and no maxLength/pattern on keys or values, and is used as the schema for find/export `filter` and for every aggregation stage that is not `$vectorSearch`. src/tools/mongodb/mongodbTool.ts:11-17 defines `DBOperationArgs.database` and `CollOperationArgs.collection` as plain `z.string()` with no length cap or character allow-list, unlike `CommonArgs.string()` (args.ts:22-23), which applies `NO_UNICODE_REGEX` and is used for the Atlas tool arguments in the same repo. mcpHttpServer.ts:307 enforces express.json({limit: httpBodyLimit}) (default 100 KiB) and result-side caps (maxDocumentsPerQuery, maxBytesPerQuery) exist, but neither validates individual field length/shape, so per-field input validation is still missing. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: Both Dockerfiles pin node:24-alpine with no content digest
description:
Dockerfile:1 and deploy/aws/Dockerfile:2 both read `FROM node:24-alpine` with no `@sha256:...` digest, so the runtime base of the image behind the order-routing critical function (applications/mcp-gateway/env/prod.json, eks-prod-mumbai) floats to whatever node:24-alpine currently resolves to at build time. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.MA.S3-mapped applicable control PR.IP.S1 (high). SLA topic: patch-sla.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Evidence holds: Dockerfile:1 and deploy/aws/Dockerfile:2 both read `FROM node:24-alpine` with no digest, and no @sha256 pin, base-image build arg or override appears anywhere else in the checkout. The SARIF export has a CICD-PIN-02 fail result at Dockerfile lines 1-1 with maxwell/v1 fingerprint 6c113f0c...5974, the same regulatory refs, invocation executionSuccessful true, revisionId equal to pinnedCommit and the same session and run. details.json links critical function order-routing to mcp-gateway, and prod.json (tier prod, exposure partner, cluster eks-prod-mumbai) points iac at this repo's deploy/ path. Severity high stands, but not for the reason the record gives: catalog PR.DS.S6 applies only to reCategories mii and qualified-re, while example-co is registered as mid-size-re. So the "catalog defaultSeverity" basis is doubtful under regulatory-mapping, and high still follows from the SARIF level error under maxwell-conventions section 4 step 3. Two further notes: deploy/aws/README.md describes that Dockerfile as a Bedrock AgentCore image pushed to ECR in us-east-1, so tying it to eks-prod-mumbai is an inference, not something the files state. And the remediation text is wrong in one place: .github/dependabot.yml already has a docker entry, but only for directory "/", so deploy/aws/Dockerfile is not covered. (Unverifiable: the export sha256 dc357366... could not be recomputed and no other recorded digest exists to compare it with.)); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (The cited clause sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 does not bind example-co: its catalog applicability is reCategories [mii, qualified-re] and its prose says 'Exempt for Mid-size, Small-size and Self-certification REs', while both of example-co's SEBI registrations are mid-size-re; no sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 control record exists in soc/main.jsonl either, so controlIds would dangle. The mapping is repairable with sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S1 (mandatory for all REs, no reCategory limit; its prose requires 'deploying only hardened and vetted hardware and software', which an unpinned floating node:24-alpine base breaks). A control record for it exists in the ledger and its defaultSeverity is high, so severity=high stays correct. SEBI stays first, and nist-ssdf-800-218 (global, empty applicability) stays as a secondary ref next to PR.IP.S1's catalog mapping nist-csf-2.0 PR.PS-01. The description text naming 'PR.DS.S6 (high)' should be updated to match. Note PR.IP.S1's probeWorkflows list does not include probe-cicd-env, but no category-unrestricted CSCRF control that does list it (PR.IP.S4 scanning, PR.MA.S3 patching) covers base-image pinning as directly.).

title: Unverified binary download in mcp-publish.yml, and deploy/aws/Dockerfile silently ignores its own version pin
description:
mcp-publish.yml:22 runs `curl -L .../mcp-publisher_...tar.gz | tar xz mcp-publisher` with no checksum or signature check, then executes that binary in a job holding `id-token: write` (mcp-publish.yml:11-13) to publish to the MCP registry. Separately, deploy/aws/Dockerfile:3 declares `ARG VERSION=latest` and labels the image `version=${VERSION}`, but deploy/aws/Dockerfile:9 hardcodes `RUN npm install -g mongodb-mcp-server@latest`, ignoring VERSION entirely -- every AWS-image rebuild installs whatever is newest on npm regardless of the version the build was supposedly pinned to. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.IP.S4 (high). SLA topic: patch-sla.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (The evidence holds, but the control mapping needs repair. mcp-publish.yml:22 really does pipe `curl -L .../latest/download/mcp-publisher_*.tar.gz` into `tar xz`, then runs `./mcp-publisher login github-oidc` and `publish` under `id-token: write`. publish.yml calls it on every new `latest` release. deploy/aws/Dockerfile:3 has `ARG VERSION=latest` and :9 hardcodes `npm install -g mongodb-mcp-server@latest`. The SARIF export has a CICD-PIN-03 fail result with the same fingerprint. sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 does not apply to example-co (mid-size-re exempt, and no control record exists for it), so the nearest applicable control is PR.IP.S4, which no reCategory filter excludes, lists probe-cicd-env and also defaults to high; severity high stands.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (The cited primary clause sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 does not bind example-co. The fix is sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S4 ("Scan critical software for malicious code"), which binds every RE except Small-size and Self-certification, has a ledger control record, and defaultSeverity high, so severity stays high. sebi-cscrf-2024 is correctly first, nist-ssdf-800-218 PW.4.1 is a valid global secondary.)

title: Policy's blocking secrets gate (gitleaks) is actually a narrower AWS-only scanner (git-secrets)
description:
company-profile/example-co/sdlc/policy.json ciGates[] declares {gate: secrets, tool: gitleaks, blocking: true, minSeverityToBlock: low}. The only secrets check in the checkout is code-health.yml:193-206 'Run git secrets', which runs `git-secrets --register-aws && git-secrets --scan` -- a different tool that with only --register-aws matches AWS key patterns and does not detect the JIRA/npm/GitHub tokens or MongoDB connection strings this repo's own workflows handle as secrets. Whether the job is a required status check cannot be confirmed because applications/mcp-gateway/repos/mongodb-mcp-server.json has no branchProtection block. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.IP.S4 (high).

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (policy.json declares a secrets gate using gitleaks with blocking true; code-health.yml lines 193-206 run git-secrets --register-aws only; SARIF export has a matching CICD-GATE-06 fail result; no compensating control (.gitleaks.toml, secret_scanning.yml) exists in the checkout.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (PR.IP.S3 is change management and does not cover a secrets-scanning gate; PR.IP.S4's guidance explicitly names secret scanning with blocking gates under probe-cicd-env, has a ledger control record, and shares the high defaultSeverity, so the ref is corrected to PR.IP.S4; iso-27001-2022 A.8.29, nist-ssdf-800-218 PW.7.2 and nist-csf-2.0 PR.PS-06 are taken from PR.IP.S4's catalog mappings.)

title: Published image is never signed or attested with cosign
description:

Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.IP.S2 (medium), cited because the nearer control sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.DS.S6 is exempt for mid-size REs. SLA topic: patch-sla.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (docker-publish.yml lines 78-89 push with provenance mode=max and sbom true and no signing step anywhere in the checkout; SARIF result CICD-SIGN-01 matches at the same fingerprint.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 does not bind example-co -- reCategories mii/qualified-re only, mid-size-re is exempt, and no control record exists for it. The nearest applicable SEBI clause is PR.IP.S2 (SDLC with security stages, mandatory, no reCategory restriction, control record present, defaultSeverity medium), so severity becomes medium. rbi-outsourcing-risk-directions-2025:97(vii) (cloud/container governance, binds nbfc-middle-layer, control record present) is a valid secondary ref after the SEBI ref; nist-ssdf-800-218 PS.2.1 is a valid global mapping.)

title: SBOM generated by CI is never captured into the workspace image inventory for mcp-gateway
description:
docker-publish.yml:87 sets `sbom: true` on the buildx build-push step, which would attach a CycloneDX/SPDX attestation to the pushed image, but no applications/mcp-gateway/images/ directory or record exists in the workspace at all -- Scout confirmed no imageId or sbomPath is linked to this repo. Per the present-but-empty-SBOM rule an SBOM step whose output is never attached, uploaded or attested to the workspace is treated as a missing SBOM. mcp-gateway's container backs the order-routing critical function (company-profile/example-co/details.json criticalFunctions[0]) and runs in prod with pii/financial data. No image record exists so this targets the repo rather than an imageId. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 GV.SC.S5 (high). SLA topic: sbom.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (docker-publish.yml line 87 sets sbom: true; no export, upload or attest step exists anywhere in the checkout; no image records exist under applications/mcp-gateway; SARIF export has a matching CICD-SBOM-02 fail result; severity high matches the GV.SC.S5 catalog defaultSeverity, whose control record exists in the ledger.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (sebi-cscrf-2024:GV.SC.S5 is in scope for example-co, exists in the catalog, covers a missing SBOM for a critical system and is cited first; its defaultSeverity is high; rbi-outsourcing-risk-directions-2025:97(vii) is a valid secondary cloud/container-governance ref with a ledger control record; nist-ssdf-800-218 PS.3.2 is a catalog mapping of GV.SC.S5.)

title: Credential issuance for the MongoDB MCP gateway's Azure Container App is disabled by the tracked default template
description: MongoDB credentials are handled correctly: main.bicep declares mdbConnectionString as @secure() (line 69) and passes it only through a Container App secretRef (lines 96-108, 157), and both tracked parameter files use the '<MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING>' placeholder rather than a literal value. But no credential is required of callers of the deployed HTTP endpoint itself: authMode defaults to 'NOAUTH' in main.bicep (line 53), which sets MDB_MCP_HTTP_AUTH_MODE=none (lines 135-140) and skips the containerAppAuth child resource (line 185, guarded by authMode == 'MicrosoftMIBasedAuth'). deploy/azure/bicep/params_template.json, the tracked default parameter file, keeps authMode: NOAUTH (line 21) and is literally named 'mongo-mcp-without-auth' (line 5). Env qa and prod both attribute this module via iac[].path 'deploy' and both classify data as pii, financial. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: Security safeguards for personal data are undermined by the default no-auth, write-enabled MCP gateway template
description: env qa and env prod both classify data as pii and financial and reside in IN. The tracked default deployment template (params_template.json) provisions the MongoDB MCP gateway with authMode NOAUTH (line 21) and MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY: 'false' (line 12), i.e. unauthenticated read+write access to personal and financial data stores if this template is used as shipped. Reasonable security safeguards under DPDP Rule 6(1)(b) require access control commensurate with the data's sensitivity; encryption/localisation (residency: IN, logsInIndia: true) are otherwise in order per env json. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: Azure AD client-application allow-list for the MCP gateway defaults to unrestricted

The tracked paramsWithAuthEnabled_template.json does populate placeholders (lines 25-27), but nothing in main.bicep enforces that the array is non-empty. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: AWS Bedrock AgentCore Dockerfile has no pinned base image or package version
description: deploy/aws/Dockerfile line 2 (`FROM node:24-alpine`) carries no digest, line 3 (`ARG VERSION=latest`) is only used to stamp a LABEL and does not pin anything actually installed, and line 9 (`RUN npm install -g mongodb-mcp-server@latest`) installs whatever the latest published mongodb-mcp-server release is at build time with no lockfile. This is inconsistent with company-profile/example-co/sdlc/policy.json dependencyPolicy.lockfilesRequired = true, and it means two builds on different days can silently ship different, unreviewed code. Severity is the sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.IP.S3 catalog defaultSeverity (sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 does not apply: example-co is registered mid-size-re and that control's applicability is limited to mii, qualified-re). First problem, the severity basis: sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.DS.S6 applies only to reCategories [mii, qualified-re], its prose says 'Exempt for Mid-size, Small-size and Self-certification REs', both example-co SEBI registrations are mid-size-re, and the ledger has no sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 control record, so controlIds would dangle; the ledger already applied the fix to fnd_01M2GH5AS0MM2F8MSFTDP36VV9, citing PR.IP.S1 (control record at main.jsonl line 76, mandatory, no reCategory limit, defaultSeverity high), so high stays. Second problem, deployment: nothing shows this AgentCore image is deployed; qa/prod run on EKS ap-south-1 (env JSONs, app README), deploy/aws/README.md pushes to ECR us-east-1 for Bedrock AgentCore, there are no image records under applications/mcp-gateway/images, and the only link is env iac[].path 'deploy', so the 'serving the same pii/financial stores' and 'production data path' wording must be softened. Also, the unpinned base image on deploy/aws/Dockerfile:2 is already recorded in open finding fnd_01M2GH5AS0MM2F8MSFTDP36VV9 (CICD-PIN-02), so only the `@latest` npm install is new here. (unverifiable: SARIF sha256 5b29e0ed... cannot be recomputed and no other recorded digest for that path exists)); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (The finding stands, but its main SEBI clause is wrong and needs fixing. sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 does not apply to example-co: the catalog limits it to mii and qualified-re ("Exempt for Mid-size, Small-size and Self-certification REs"), both of example-co's SEBI registrations are mid-size-re, the ledger has no control record for PR.DS.S6, and probe-iac is not one of its probe workflows. Earlier refuter verdicts in the ledger (lines 701 and 706) already said the same. The fix is sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S3 (configuration change control and change management). It covers mii, qualified-re and mid-size-re, lists probe-iac with guidance on infrastructure drift outside the pipeline, has a control record at ledger line 78, and has defaultSeverity high, so severity stays high. Crosswalks should come from PR.IP.S3's catalog mappings: nist-ssdf PS.2.1 and ISO A.8.30 are only PR.DS.S6 mappings, and A.8.30 (outsourced development) does not fit this gap. SEBI is correctly listed first, and sebi-cscrf-2024, iso-27001-2022 and nist-ssdf-800-218 all apply to example-co. The Dockerfile lines 2, 3 and 9 match the description. I did not check the patch-sla topic or the SLA, because the ledger keeper computes slaBasis later; I also did not open the SARIF export, because this lens does not need it.).

title: mcp-gateway's HTTP transport (/mcp) has no default authentication
description: src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts setupMiddlewares() (lines 306-319) is the only gate on the /mcp POST/GET/DELETE routes (lines 360-411), which reach every registered MongoDB and Atlas tool including insert-many, delete-many, drop-collection, drop-database and connect. It loops over userConfig.httpHeaders and rejects a request only when a configured header/value pair is missing; httpHeaders defaults to {} (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:136-143, overrideBehavior 'not-allowed') and server.json documents --httpHeaders/MDB_MCP_HTTP_HEADERS as an optional, non-secret setting. With no operator configuration, every /mcp request is served with zero authentication. streamableHttp.ts (shouldWarnAboutHttpHost) only logs a warning when httpHost is non-loopback; it enforces nothing. mcp-gateway's qa and prod environments run this server on EKS ap-south-1 with dataClassification [pii, financial]; prod exposure is 'partner'. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.AA.S17. SLA topic: patch-sla. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every cited fact is in the files: mcpHttpServer.ts 306-319 checks only userConfig.httpHeaders and /mcp POST/GET/DELETE are at 360-411; userConfig.ts 136-143 defaults httpHeaders to {} with overrideBehavior not-allowed; server.json marks MDB_MCP_HTTP_HEADERS and --httpHeaders isRequired false and isSecret false; shouldWarnAboutHttpHost only logs; the tools insert-many, delete-many, drop-collection, drop-database and connect exist; nothing else in src/transports does auth; the in-repo deploy files add none for EKS (the AWS Dockerfile binds 0.0.0.0 with no headers, its bearer token belongs to Bedrock AgentCore, and Azure defaults to NOAUTH); prod.json shows partner exposure and [pii, financial], qa.json shows qa on EKS ap-south-1 with the same classification; the SARIF export has a SCH-API-01 fail result at the same path and lines with maxwell/v1 fingerprint equal to the candidate's; high matches the PR.AA.S17 catalog defaultSeverity. Style only: evidence[0] and evidence[2] both point at the same SARIF export and should be one entry carrying the sha256. (unverifiable: the SARIF sha256 cannot be computed here, but it matches the context sarifSha256; no EKS manifests or values in the workspace show whether prod sets httpHeaders or has an ingress/mesh auth layer, and the finding is correctly framed as a code-default gap.)); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (The mapping holds: sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.AA.S17 (API authentication, authorisation and access management so only intended entities reach APIs) and dpdp-rules-2025 6(1)(b) (access control on computer resources) both exist in their catalogs, both are in example-co's frameworksInScope, and PR.AA.S17's reCategories cover the company's active mid-size-re SEBI registrations. Both control records exist in the ledger, and prod.json confirms the pii data classification, so the DPDP ref applies. SEBI is cited first as the most specific Indian instrument, since the app supports order routing for the broker. The SARIF export has no security-severity or CVSS score, so severity high correctly comes from PR.AA.S17's catalog defaultSeverity (high). Non-blocking note: the global ref owasp-asvs-5.0 8.2.1 is not among PR.AA.S17's catalog mappings (the catalog maps ASVS V4, plus nist-csf-2.0 PR.AA-05 and cis-controls-8.1 16.13), and there is no ASVS catalog to check the 8.2.1 wording against. It is a secondary ref from an instrument that applies to everyone, so it does not refute. Optional: company is also an RBI NBFC with rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026 in scope, so an RBI access-control clause could be added as a secondary ref (unverifiable: ASVS 5.0 8.2.1 text).).

title: Open EJSON filter/pipeline/document arguments and unbounded database/collection names reach the MongoDB driver directly
description: zEJSON() (src/tools/args.ts:86-90) is z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON) with no keys, maxItems, maxLength or pattern, and is reused unmodified as the filter argument on find (find.ts) and delete-many (deleteMany.ts), the pipeline argument on aggregate (mongodbSchemas.ts/aggregate.ts), the documents argument on insert-many (insertMany.ts: z.array(zEJSON())), and the exportTarget.arguments on export (export.ts). CollOperationArgs.database/.collection (mongodbTool.ts:11-18) are plain z.string() with no bound. All flow straight into the mongosh service-provider driver (provider.find/aggregate/insertMany/deleteMany) with no further schema-level validation; the only backstops are the operator-configured maxBytesPerQuery/maxDocumentsPerQuery caps and the confirmationRequiredTools elicitation list (userConfig.ts:79-94), which excludes insert-many and update-many. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.IP.S2. SLA topic: patch-sla. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (The evidence holds up: the SARIF export has an SCH-API-02 fail result at src/tools/args.ts:86-90 with the same message, controls and fingerprint as the candidate. The checkout shows the same code: zEJSON() = z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON), used by find, delete-many, update-many, insert-many (z.array), aggregate (AnyAggregateStage) and export. database and collection are plain z.string(). The values reach provider.find/aggregate/insertMany/deleteMany. confirmationRequiredTools defaults leave out insert-many and update-many. Nothing in the repo cancels this: readOnly and indexCheck are off by default, and deploy/aws/Dockerfile only disables atlas-local. prod.json runs on AWS EKS with partner exposure, so the gap is reachable. medium equals the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.IP.S2 and of dpdp-rules-2025 6(1)(g). A small omission, not grounds to refute: the description skips runtime guards that operators can turn on (readOnly, disabledTools, and aggregate's check that blocks $out/$merge when writes are disabled). These are runtime checks, not schema bounds. PR.IP.S2 is an SDLC control and a loose fit for input validation, but that belongs to the regulatory-mapping lens. (unverifiable: the export sha256 ac53f2a6... cannot be recomputed here.)); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (The mapping holds. Both Indian instruments apply to example-co: sebi-cscrf-2024 and dpdp-rules-2025 are in frameworksInScope, the company is a stock broker and DP registered as a mid-size RE, and dpdp-rules-2025 lists both entity types. The SEBI control PR.IP.S2 is cited first; it exists, has no reCategory restriction, and its prose asks for an SSDLC with data-integrity requirements and OWASP ASVS guidance, which covers unbounded schemas reaching the MongoDB driver. Severity medium is correct: the SCH-API-02 rule has no security-severity score, so the catalog defaultSeverity of PR.IP.S2 (medium) applies. The controlIds match maxwell/controlIds on the SARIF result at src/tools/args.ts:86-90, and ledger control records exist for both. Minor notes, none reason to refute: (1) PR.IP.S6 (secure coding practices, also medium, also in the ledger) would be a slightly tighter SEBI clause; (2) the 6(1)(g) guidance says findings there usually accompany a pattern of gaps rather than one technical defect, and DPDP Rules take effect 2027-05-13, after now, so it can only be a secondary readiness ref, which is where it sits. Unverifiable: owasp-asvs-5.0 2.2.1 has no local catalog, and SLA fields were not checked, as instructed.).
